title: Feature Ticket Specification
description: Structured output from Business Analyst. Consumed by Technical Architect (for adr-spec.json), Technical Lead (for technical-delivery-plan.json), and Backend/Frontend Developers as the source of truth for scope, acceptance criteria, and business rules. Also optionally triggers Data Analyst and SEO Analyst handoffs. For AI/LLM features, includes ai_feature_spec (probabilistic AC, HITL triggers, EU AI Act tier) and assumption_register (risk-scored assumptions).

ticket_id.description: Unique identifier. Convention: YYYY-MM-DD-short-slug or project-number.

business_value.description: Why this work matters to the business or users. Expressed as outcome, not activity.

preserved_behavior.description: Behavior that must remain unchanged after this change. Required for bug fixes.

changed_behavior.description: Intended new or restored behavior. Expressed in user/system terms.

actors.description: Human users, systems, or agent roles involved in this feature.

business_rules.description: Explicit business rules and invariants. Each rule must be testable.

rule.description: The business rule, stated as a declarative sentence.

exceptions.description: Known exceptions or edge cases to this rule.

acceptance_criteria.description: Testable acceptance scenarios in Given/When/Then format. For AI features, use ai_feature_spec for probabilistic AC — do not encode statistical thresholds in this plain GWT format.

scenario.description: Short label for this AC scenario.

edge_cases.description: Edge cases that require special handling but aren't full AC scenarios.

dependencies.description: Other tickets, services, or teams this work depends on.

out_of_scope.description: Explicitly excluded from this ticket to prevent scope creep.

open_questions.description: Questions requiring clarification before or during implementation.

process_impact.description: Downstream teams, systems, workflows, or users affected beyond the core change.

ai_feature_spec.description: Required when the feature involves AI/LLM behavior. Owned by Business Analyst. Consumed by Technical Lead, QA Engineer, and Reviewer as AI acceptance criteria evidence. Binary pass/fail AC must NOT be used for AI features — use this block instead.

behavioral_boundaries.description: Acceptable output range expressed as intent — not exact string match. E.g. 'Response must be professional in tone, contain no hallucinated product names, and cite only verified sources.'

probabilistic_ac.description: Statistical acceptance criteria for AI behavior. Replaces binary pass/fail for non-deterministic outputs.

threshold_pct.description: Minimum percentage of correct outcomes. E.g. 95 means ≥95% of N samples must meet the criteria.

population.description: The population or input distribution this threshold applies to.

window_n.description: Sample window size for threshold evaluation (e.g. 100 evaluations per week).

judge.description: Who or what acts as the judge — specify model name, rubric reference, or reviewer role.

hitl_trigger.description: Human-in-the-Loop escalation specification. Required for any AI feature with high-stakes decisions (financial, legal, medical, safety, access control). AI-HITL-SPEC LOCK applies.

condition.description: When does AI autonomy end? E.g. 'confidence_score < 0.85' or 'decision_category = credit'.

action.description: What happens when the trigger fires? E.g. 'pause decision, display Under Review status'.

sla.description: Maximum response time after escalation. E.g. '24h', '4h for safety-critical'.

audit_log_required.description: Whether an immutable audit log must be written at the escalation point.

audit_log_fields.description: Fields required in the audit log: e.g. model_version, input_summary, output, confidence, human_decision, timestamp.

non_determinism.description: deterministic_required: identical inputs must produce identical outputs (temperature=0 or equivalent). controlled_variation: intentional A/B or seeded variation. creative_generation: open-ended generation acceptable.

hybrid_architecture_intent.description: Which components use deterministic rule-based logic vs AI/LLM? High-stakes actions (payment, legal notice, access revocation) must be deterministic.

accountability_model.description: Who owns AI decisions and how are they monitored post-launch.

decision_owner.description: Accountable role for AI decisions in this feature.

monitoring_metric.description: KPI or metric used to detect degradation in production.

review_cadence.description: How often AI behavior is reviewed post-launch. E.g. 'weekly for 4 weeks, then monthly'.

audit_log_requirements.description: Immutable audit log spec: fields required per AI decision (model version, input summary, output, confidence, human intervention).

eu_ai_act_tier.description: EU AI Act risk tier classification. high-risk requires HITL, audit logging, conformity assessment, and Human Review Board availability. Must be classified before AC is locked.

degradation_trigger.description: Production degradation alert spec. E.g. 'If accuracy falls below 90% in any 7-day rolling window, raise P1 incident and suspend feature pending review.'

assumption_register.description: Risk-scored assumptions that underlie the requirements. Required for significant bets. Risk score = impact × (6 − confidence). Highest-risk assumptions must be validated before build commitment. ASSUMPTION LOCK applies.

assumption.description: What must be true for this requirement to be valid? State as a declarative belief.

impact.description: If this assumption is wrong, how bad is the outcome? 1=trivial, 5=project-breaking.

confidence.description: How much evidence supports this assumption being true? 1=pure guess, 5=verified fact.

risk_score.description: Computed as impact × (6 − confidence). Range 1–25. Scores ≥15 require validation before build commitment.

validation_method.description: How will this assumption be validated? E.g. 'user interview', 'analytics query', 'spike', 'legal review'.

status.description: Current validation status. escalated = PM notified with build-cost comparison.

outcome_note.description: Result of validation or reason for escalation. Required when status is validated/invalidated/escalated.

analytics_request.description: Optional handoff block for Data Analyst — triggers data investigation request.

decision_supported.description: What business decision will this data inform?

seo_content_request.description: Optional handoff block for SEO Analyst — triggers content or discoverability work.

must_link_to.description: High-value paths (product, property, guides) BA wants emphasized.

research_request.description: Optional handoff block for Researcher — triggers domain or compliance research. depth must align with researcher.md depth_mode: deep (10+ rounds, default) or scoped (3+ rounds, requires scope_waiver_note).

research_question.description: Primary research question (singular framing). Use questions[] for numbered multi-part requests.

questions.description: Numbered research questions and boundaries. Preferred over research_question for multi-part requests.

depth.description: deep: 10+ research rounds (default). scoped: minimum 3 rounds — requires scope_waiver_note explaining why deep is not needed.

scope_waiver_note.description: Required when depth = scoped. Explains why deep discovery is not needed for this request.

output_contract.description: Expected output format from Researcher. research-report.json for machine handoff; markdown-brief for quick synthesis.

ai_interaction_requirements.description: 2026 PM Standard: Define HITL and fallback bounds.

examples.title: Change Order Assignment Logic for COD Store Orders
examples.business_value: Reduce failed COD delivery assignments by routing store orders to the nearest active store with COD capability, instead of the default warehouse courier route.
examples.preserved_behavior: Non-COD orders continue to use existing auto-assign logic unchanged.
examples.changed_behavior: COD orders with a store_id set are routed to the store's designated courier, bypassing warehouse assignment.

business_rules.rule: A COD order with store_id must be assigned to a courier linked to that store.
business_rules.exceptions: If no active courier is linked to the store, fall back to warehouse assignment and log a warning.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: COD order assigned to store courier
acceptance_criteria.given: A COD order exists with store_id=42 and store 42 has an active courier
acceptance_criteria.then: The order is assigned to the store 42 courier, not the warehouse courier

acceptance_criteria.scenario: COD order with no store courier falls back
acceptance_criteria.given: A COD order exists with store_id=99 and store 99 has no active courier
acceptance_criteria.then: The order is assigned to the warehouse courier and a warning is logged
The order follows the existing auto-assign logic without entering the new branch

edge_cases: store_id is set but store record is soft-deleted
COD order arrives during store courier capacity blackout window

assumption_register.assumption: Store courier lookup API returns results within 200ms p99 under current load
assumption_register.validation_method: Load test against staging Store service API with 2x current peak traffic

assumption_register.assumption: Store Manager team will accept new courier assignment notifications without process change
assumption_register.validation_method: Interview 3 Store Managers before sprint planning
assumption_register.outcome_note: Confirmed in stakeholder session 2026-06-10 — Store Managers prefer automated routing

dependencies: Store service API for courier lookup
open_questions: Should we notify the store manager when fallback occurs?
examples.process_impact: Store operations team will see different courier assignments for COD orders starting from deploy date.

questions: What are the industry-standard SLA expectations for COD store courier assignment in Southeast Asian e-commerce platforms?
Are there regulatory requirements for COD assignment logging in Vietnam logistics regulations 2026?
research_request.domain: SEA e-commerce logistics, Vietnam COD regulations
research_request.scope_waiver_note: Domain is narrow and well-defined; 3 targeted research passes sufficient before locking courier SLA AC.

examples.title: AI Credit Scoring Assistant for Loan Applications
examples.business_value: Reduce manual credit review time by 40% while maintaining accuracy above 95% through AI-assisted preliminary scoring with mandatory human confirmation for all decisions.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: AI score produced with high confidence
acceptance_criteria.given: A complete loan application with all required fields
acceptance_criteria.when: The AI scoring service processes the application
acceptance_criteria.then: A preliminary score and confidence rating are produced within 3 seconds

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Low-confidence application routed to human review
acceptance_criteria.given: AI confidence score < 0.85 for any application
acceptance_criteria.then: Application is paused, status set to Under Review, and Credit Officer notified within 15 minutes

ai_feature_spec.behavioral_boundaries: AI must produce a credit score band (A/B/C/D/F) and confidence score. It must not approve or reject loans autonomously. All preliminary scores require Credit Officer confirmation. Response must contain no hallucinated applicant data and must reference only verified financial fields from the application.

probabilistic_ac.population: Complete loan applications passing input validation
probabilistic_ac.judge: Senior Credit Officer panel reviewing 200 sampled applications weekly against ground truth

hitl_trigger.condition: AI confidence score < 0.85 OR loan_amount > 500,000,000 VND OR applicant_category = 'first-time-borrower'
hitl_trigger.action: Pause decision, set status to 'Under Review', notify assigned Credit Officer via in-app alert and email
hitl_trigger.responsible_role: Credit Officer (primary), Risk Manager (escalation if no response in 8h)
hitl_trigger.sla: Credit Officer must confirm or override within 24h; Risk Manager escalation within 32h

ai_feature_spec.hybrid_architecture_intent: AI/LLM handles preliminary scoring and risk factor summarization only. Deterministic rule engine handles: final approval/rejection execution, rate calculation, regulatory compliance checks, and all database writes for approved loans.

accountability_model.decision_owner: Credit Officer (all decisions); Risk Manager (escalated decisions); VP Credit (policy exceptions)
accountability_model.monitoring_metric: Weekly accuracy rate vs ground truth; HITL trigger rate; Credit Officer override rate
accountability_model.review_cadence: Weekly for first 8 weeks post-launch, then bi-weekly; quarterly model performance review
accountability_model.audit_log_requirements: Immutable append-only log per decision: model_version, input_field_hash, ai_score_band, ai_confidence, human_decision, override_reason, timestamps. Retained 7 years per financial regulation.

ai_feature_spec.degradation_trigger: If weekly accuracy rate falls below 93% for any 7-day window, raise P1 incident, suspend AI scoring (revert to fully manual), and notify Risk Manager and VP Credit within 2h.

assumption_register.assumption: Credit Officers will adopt AI-assisted workflow without significant process resistance
assumption_register.validation_method: Structured interview with 5 Credit Officers + 2-week pilot with shadow mode (AI scores hidden from officers until after their decision)
assumption_register.outcome_note: Risk score 20 — escalated to PM 2026-06-12. Pilot proposed before sprint commitment. Build commitment deferred pending pilot results.

assumption_register.assumption: AI model accuracy ≥95% is achievable with current training data volume (12 months)
assumption_register.validation_method: Offline evaluation on 6-month holdout dataset before feature build starts

out_of_scope: AI model training and retraining pipeline
Regulatory filing for EU AI Act conformity assessment
open_questions: Has legal confirmed EU AI Act high-risk classification and conformity assessment timeline?
Who is the designated Human Review Board required under EU AI Act Article 14?
